notes.n1.eda: Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens hold the large majority of the market; a funded wave of AI-native design startups emerged in 2025-26 (ChipAgents, Cognichip, Ricursive); China pushes domestic EDA.
notes.n1.ip: Arm dominates CPU IP; RISC-V vendors grow; interconnect/SerDes IP consolidated (Qualcomm-Alphawave, GF bought MIPS and Synopsys ARC).
notes.n1.equip: ASML (EUV monopoly), Applied, Lam, TEL and KLA dominate; Chinese vendors (Naura, AMEC) grow under export controls; HBM drives demand for bonders (Hanmi, Besi, ASMPT).
notes.n1.materials: Japanese suppliers dominate wafers, resists and ABF substrates; substrate and T-glass capacity are AI bottlenecks.
notes.n1.foundry: TSMC makes nearly all leading-edge AI accelerators; Samsung, Intel (14A) and Rapidus are the alternatives; SMIC serves China's domestic accelerators; India's first fab (Tata-PSMC) under construction.
notes.n1.packaging: TSMC CoWoS capacity is the main AI packaging bottleneck; ASE/SPIL and Amkor are the main OSAT overflow; India OSATs (CG Semi, Micron, Kaynes, Tata) started production in 2025-26.
notes.n1.memory: HBM is a three-player market (SK hynix leads, Samsung, Micron); CXMT is developing Chinese HBM; NAND/SSD demand rising for inference KV-cache tiers.
notes.n1.design: Broadcom and Marvell lead custom AI ASIC programmes for hyperscalers; Taiwanese design houses (Alchip, GUC, MediaTek) take TSMC-aligned work.
notes.n1.masks: Mask blanks dominated by Japanese suppliers (HOYA, AGC, Shin-Etsu); leading-edge masks largely captive at foundries
notes.n1.yield: KLA dominates inspection; PDF Solutions leads independent yield analytics
